styles.noir_macro: Straight documentary macro photography. A single hard key light rakes across the subject from one side and everything outside its throw falls to genuine black — no fill, no bounce, no softbox wash. Shot on a fast macro prime with shallow depth of field: one narrow plane is critically sharp and the rest melts away. Real physical materials with visible microscopic texture — machined metal, oxidation, wear, dust suspended in the beam. Fine natural film grain, subtle lens vignette, slight halation on the brightest speculars. Restrained and near-monochrome. No digital gloss, no HDR, no over-sharpening, no plastic CGI look.
styles.tech_noir: Cinematic tech-noir still. The subject is carved out of darkness by a strong coloured rim light with a second opposing kicker on the far side, faint atmospheric haze holding visible shafts of that light, and a wet black glass surface beneath throwing a short soft mirrored reflection that fades out completely well above the bottom of the frame. Gentle anamorphic bloom on the brightest specular edges, deep crushed blacks. The saturated colour lives entirely in the LIGHT — every surface and material stays neutral and unpainted. Photoreal and razor sharp: a title still from a financial thriller, not an illustration.
styles.archive_still: Fine-art still-life photography in the chiaroscuro tradition. One large soft key from high and to one side, hard-flagged so the falloff into shadow is fast and smooth, and no fill at all. A seamless deep-charcoal sweep behind, a matte tabletop, no haze, no flare, no visible light source. The MATERIALS carry the drama — aged brass, oxidised steel, cracked glass, heavy paper, settled dust — rendered with immaculate detail and quiet restraint. Museum object photography: still, evidential, expensive. Photoreal, edge-to-edge sharp on the subject, deep shadow everywhere else.

blueprints: One hard key light from the upper left grazing along the surfaces, picking out every machined edge, tooling mark and thread. A faint cool ambient lifts the shadow side just enough to read.
cold gunmetal, brushed steel and blue-grey over near-black, with one restrained steel-blue or cyan highlight. Almost no warmth. Precise and engineered.
valueTraps: One low warm key from the right, plus a deep red ambient wash bleeding into the shadows behind the subject so the darkness itself is coloured.
oxblood, rust and burnished copper-red over a warm red-black. Rich, dark and restrained — never bright, never scarlet, never a pure saturated red.
battles: TWO opposing key lights of equal strength and opposite temperature: a cold steel-blue key from the left and a warm amber key from the right, meeting on the subject so one side of it is cold and the other warm, with the division clearly visible. Everything beyond them falls to black.
cold steel-blue on one side against warm amber and old gold on the other, over a neutral near-black. Exactly two hues plus black — no third colour anywhere.
